title: Coffee on Satou-san
setting: A Saturday afternoon in an old coffee shop near the station. Yuki ran into her elderly neighbour Satou-san on the shopping street and helped carry his bags, and he took her for a coffee at the place he has been going to for years. Over coffee he has some news, and when it is time to leave he has a surprise for her.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: satou-san, kono omise, hajimete kimashita. igokochi ga ii desu ne.
lines.ja: 佐藤さん、このお店、初めて来ました。居心地がいいですね。
lines.kana: さとうさん、このおみせ、はじめてきました。いごこちがいいですね。
lines.english: Satou-san, this is my first time in here. It's really cosy.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou deshou. mukashi kara, yoku kuru n desu yo.
lines.ja: そうでしょう。昔から、よく来るんですよ。
lines.kana: そうでしょう。むかしから、よくくるんですよ。
lines.english: Isn't it? I've been coming here for years.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, koohii, roppyaku en mo suru n desu ne.
lines.ja: あ、コーヒー、六百円もするんですね。
lines.kana: あ、コーヒー、ろっぴゃくえんもするんですね。
lines.english: Oh, the coffee's a whole six hundred yen.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: nedan wa chotto takai kedo, oishii n desu yo.
lines.ja: 値段はちょっと高いけど、おいしいんですよ。
lines.kana: ねだんはちょっとたかいけど、おいしいんですよ。
lines.english: It's a bit pricey, but it's good, you know.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: honto da, oishii! kore nara, nedan ga chotto takakute mo, mata kitai desu.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、おいしい！これなら、値段がちょっと高くても、また来たいです。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、おいしい！これなら、ねだんがちょっとたかくても、またきたいです。
lines.english: It really is good! For coffee like this, I'd come back even if it is a bit pricey.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou ieba, yuki-san. watashi, saikin piano o naratteru n desu yo.
lines.ja: そういえば、ユキさん。私、最近ピアノを習ってるんですよ。
lines.kana: そういえば、ゆきさん。わたし、さいきんピアノをならってるんですよ。
lines.english: Oh, that reminds me, Yuki-san. I've been taking piano lessons lately.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sugoi desu ne! demo, piano tte, kekkou okane kakarimasen ka?
lines.ja: え、すごいですね！でも、ピアノって、けっこうお金かかりませんか？
lines.kana: え、すごいですね！でも、ピアノって、けっこうおかねかかりませんか？
lines.english: Wow, that's amazing! But doesn't piano cost quite a lot?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou desu ne, okane wa kakarimasu. tsuki ni ichiman en harattemasu.
lines.ja: そうですね、お金はかかります。月に一万円払ってます。
lines.kana: そうですね、おかねはかかります。つきにいちまんえんはらってます。
lines.english: Well, yes, it does cost money. I pay ten thousand yen a month.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ichiman en! piano tte, ikura suru n desu ka?
lines.ja: 一万円！ピアノって、いくらするんですか？
lines.kana: いちまんえん！ピアノって、いくらするんですか？
lines.english: Ten thousand yen! And how much is a piano?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: atarashii no wa, gojuuman en mo shimasu yo. demo, uchi no wa, kodomo ga mukashi tsukatteta piano na n desu.
lines.ja: 新しいのは、五十万円もしますよ。でも、うちのは、子どもが昔使ってたピアノなんです。
lines.kana: あたらしいのは、ごじゅうまんえんもしますよ。でも、うちのは、こどもがむかしつかってたピアノなんです。
lines.english: A new one costs a good five hundred thousand yen. But ours is the piano my children used to play years ago.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, piano ni wa okane kakaranakatta n desu ne. yokatta desu ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ピアノにはお金かからなかったんですね。よかったですね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ピアノにはおかねかからなかったんですね。よかったですね。
lines.english: So the piano itself didn't cost you anything. That's lucky.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sou na n desu. sorosoro kaerimashou ka.
lines.ja: そうなんです。そろそろ帰りましょうか。
lines.kana: そうなんです。そろそろかえりましょうか。
lines.english: That's right. Well, shall we head home?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ne.
lines.ja: はい。今日は割り勘にしましょうね。
lines.kana: はい。きょうはわりかんにしましょうね。
lines.english: OK. Let's split it today, all right?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: iya iya, okane wa mou haraimashita yo. sakki, toire ni itta toki ni.
lines.ja: いやいや、お金はもう払いましたよ。さっき、トイレに行ったときに。
lines.kana: いやいや、おかねはもうはらいましたよ。さっき、トイレにいったときに。
lines.english: Oh no, no. I've already paid. Earlier, when I went to the toilet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? mou, satou-san! jaa, watashi no koohii no okane dake demo harawasete kudasai.
lines.ja: え？もう、佐藤さん！じゃあ、私のコーヒーのお金だけでも払わせてください。
lines.kana: え？もう、さとうさん！じゃあ、わたしのコーヒーのおかねだけでもはらわせてください。
lines.english: What? Oh, Satou-san! Then at least let me pay for my coffee.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ii n desu yo. itsumo kaimono o tetsudatte morattemasu kara.
lines.ja: いいんですよ。いつも買い物を手伝ってもらってますから。
lines.kana: いいんですよ。いつもかいものをてつだってもらってますから。
lines.english: It's fine. You're always helping me with my shopping.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tsugi wa zettai, warikan ni shimashou ne!
lines.ja: 次は絶対、割り勘にしましょうね！
lines.kana: つぎはぜったい、わりかんにしましょうね！
lines.english: Next time we're definitely splitting it, OK?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hai hai. demo tsugi mo, toire ni iku kamo shiremasen yo.
lines.ja: はいはい。でも次も、トイレに行くかもしれませんよ。
lines.kana: はいはい。でもつぎも、トイレにいくかもしれませんよ。
lines.english: Yes, yes. Though I may need the toilet next time, too.

choices.english: Over coffee, Satou-san tells Yuki about his piano lessons, and it turns out he has already paid for both of them.
Satou-san tells Yuki about the new piano he bought, and they split the bill for their coffee.
Yuki treats Satou-san to coffee, but he insists on splitting the bill.

questions.explanation: Line 6: Satou-san says he has been taking piano lessons lately. In line 13 Yuki suggests splitting the bill (kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ne), but in line 14 he says he has already paid, when he went to the toilet. B is wrong twice: the piano isn't new, it's the one his children played years ago (line 10), and they don't split the bill. C swaps who did what: Yuki is the one who wants to split, and Satou-san has paid for both of them.

questions.english: Kenta says he's thinking of buying a car. Warn him that having a car costs quite a lot.
questions.answer: Warn him about the overall cost with okane ga kakaru, casually since it's Kenta (the ga often drops): kuruma tte kekkou okane kakaru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: e, kuruma tte kekkou okane kakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: え、車ってけっこうお金かかるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Hm, cars cost quite a bit, you know.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii kedo, kuruma motsu to okane kakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいけど、車持つとお金かかるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure, but having a car costs money.

questions.explanation: Having a car costs money overall (petrol, parking, repairs), so the verb is kakaru, as when Yuki asks whether piano costs a lot (line 7: kekkou okane kakarimasen ka?) and Satou-san answers okane wa kakarimasu (line 8). The car's price tag on its own would take suru: kuruma tte ikura suru no? (compare lines 9-10). Japanese has no single verb for 'cost', and kosuto suru isn't said.

questions.english: After hearing what the lessons cost, Yuki asks about the price of a piano. What did she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、ピアノについて何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、ピアノについてなんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, piano ni tsuite nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: How much does a piano cost? (word for word)
choices.romaji: piano wa, ikura kosuto shimasu ka?

choices.english: How much does piano cost you, all in?
choices.romaji: piano tte, ikura kakaru n desu ka?
piano tte, ikura suru n desu ka?

questions.explanation: Line 9: ichiman en! piano tte, ikura suru n desu ka? A single thing's price takes suru, and Satou-san answers in the same frame: gojuuman en mo shimasu (line 10). B uses the verb for overall spending: kakaru is what Yuki used for the lessons in line 7 (okane kakarimasen ka?), the running cost of doing piano, not what one piano goes for. A is English 'cost' word for word. kosuto is a business word for expenses, and Japanese never uses it as a verb for a price.

questions.english: After tasting the coffee, what does Yuki say about it?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、コーヒーを飲んで、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、コーヒーをのんで、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, koohii o nonde, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It's cheaper than she expected, so she'll come again.
It's a bit pricey, but it's so good she'd come back anyway.
It's good, but too pricey for her to come back.

questions.explanation: Line 5: kore nara, nedan ga chotto takakute mo, mata kitai desu. nedan ga takai means the price is high, and -te mo means 'even if', so the price doesn't put her off. Satou-san had just said nedan wa chotto takai kedo, oishii n desu yo (line 4). A gets the price backwards: the coffee is roppyaku en mo (a whole 600 yen, line 3), and a low price would be yasui. C catches takai but misses -te mo ... mata kitai: she does want to come again.

questions.english: You're at a café with Kenta. While he was in the toilet, you paid the bill. Now he says "Right, shall we head off?" and gets out his wallet. Tell him you've already paid.
questions.ja: じゃあ、そろそろ帰ろうか。
questions.kana: じゃあ、そろそろかえろうか。
questions.answer: Say it's done, with harau in the past: okane wa mou haratta yo. Keep it casual, since it's Kenta.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, okane wa mou haratta yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、お金はもう払ったよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu, okane wa sakki haratta kara.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫、お金はさっき払ったから。

questions.explanation: Handing money over is harau, and the past haratta says it's done, just as Satou-san tells Yuki in line 14 (okane wa mou haraimashita yo, sakki, toire ni itta toki ni). Don't say kaeshita: kaesu is paying back money you borrowed. Offering to pay is more often dasu (koko wa watashi ga dasu yo), and treating someone is ogoru.

questions.english: You've had dinner with Kenta. He looks at the bill and says it comes to four thousand yen altogether. Suggest splitting it evenly.
questions.kana: ぜんぶでよんせんえんだって。
questions.romaji: zenbu de yonsen en da tte.
questions.answer: Suggest it with warikan ni shiyou, and add each person's share if you like: hitori nisen en ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, warikan ni shiyou. hitori nisen en ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、割り勘にしよう。一人二千円ね。
modelAnswers.english: OK, let's split it. Two thousand each.

modelAnswers.romaji: kyou wa warikan ni shiyou ka.
modelAnswers.ja: 今日は割り勘にしようか。

questions.explanation: Splitting a bill evenly is one noun, warikan, with ni suru, as in Yuki's kyou wa warikan ni shimashou ne (line 13) and tsugi wa zettai, warikan ni shimashou ne! (line 17). English 'split' leads to wakeru, which is for asking staff for separate bills (kaikei wakete moraemasu ka?). Each person paying for their own is betsubetsu.

newWords.english: month (tsuki ni ichiman en = ten thousand yen a month)
when, at the time (toire ni itta toki ni = when I went to the toilet)
